Subject: Success criteria & acceptance tests — Redwood pilot (AcmeHealth)

Team,

Thanks again for the demo last week. Our pilot committee asked for a concise list of success criteria, concrete acceptance tests, and proposed exit gates that will determine whether we move to dedicated capacity.

High-level asks:
- Define 5–7 measurable success metrics (latency, cost per 1k tokens, accuracy on domain QA, UAT pass rate, uptime)
- Provide sample acceptance tests we can run with our dataset (include pass/fail thresholds)
- State clear exit gates (go/no-go) and a proposed close timeline with owners

Can you share a draft MAP we can review at our steering meeting next Thursday (Mar 11)?

Thanks,
Mike

--
Mike Jenkins
Director, Clinical AI
Acme Health
mike.jenkins@acmehealth.com
(415) 555-0198

From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai>

Cc: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, Mar 02, 2027 at 09:04 AM -07:00
Subject: Re: Success criteria & acceptance tests — Redwood pilot (AcmeHealth)

Mike — thanks for the clear ask. Attached is a first-pass MAP (MAP-draft-v1.xlsx) and a short runbook inline below.

Summary (top-level):
- Success metrics (measurable):
  1) 95th percentile response latency < 350ms for 1–2k token prompts (95th measured over 24h production-like runs)
  2) Average cost per 1k tokens <= $0.60 (target; allows for quantized model variant)
  3) Domain QA concordance >= 88% on the provided test set (we include sample tests)
  4) UAT pass rate >= 90% (end-users accept outputs in blind review)
  5) Platform availability >= 99.5% during pilot window

- Exit gates (go/no-go decision points):
  A) GO if metrics 1–4 meet targets for two consecutive weekly runs and no critical security gaps are open
  B) NO-GO if any of the following: domain QA concordance < 80%, 95th pct latency > 500ms, or repeated model hallucination > 10% on closed-set tests

- Acceptance tests (examples):
  • Latency: synthetic replay of 10k prior requests in staging with production-sized KV cache enabled; measure 95th pct
  • Cost: run billing-simulated workload for 48hrs with realistic token distribution (we'll provide a template)
  • Accuracy: blind evaluation on 250 labeled domain examples (we'll annotate pass/fail per sample; threshold = 88%)
  • UAT: 20 clinical reviewers label outputs for relevance/accuracy; pass if >= 90% positive

- Owners & timeline (draft):
  - Redwood: provide MAP + test harness (Hannah, Jordan) — deliver 03/03
  - Acme: supply annotated sample set and access to staging endpoints (Mike) — deliver 03/05
  - Joint: run 48–72h acceptance runs (week of 03/08)
  - Steering review & sign-off: target 03/11 (Mike & committee)

Attachments: MAP-draft-v1.xlsx (spreadsheet with metrics, owners, and a proposed run schedule). I also put a placeholder drive link in the file.

Next steps: Jordan and I will run the first acceptance harness on Wed/Thu and share the raw logs + summarized pass/fail. Can you confirm Acme can deliver the annotated 250 examples by EOD 03/05?

Thanks,
Hannah

--
Hannah Schmitt
Manager, Solutions — Redwood Inference
hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai

Thanks Hannah — quick clarifying items from engineering before we lock numbers: 

1) Latency baseline: is the 95th pct measured with model seq len = 1–2k tokens and cold KV cache allowed, or assuming warmed cache? Our internal benchmarks vary ~60–90ms depending on cache warmness. Proposal: measure both cold (first 1k requests) and warmed (next 9k) and require the warmed 95th < 350ms; cold 95th < 700ms.

2) Cost: our per-1k token number depends on quantization profile and batching policy. Can we set a tolerated band (e.g., $0.45–0.75) and tie the lower bound to an agreed quantization profile in the MAP?

3) Domain QA concordance: is the 88% threshold strict? For fairness, suggest reporting two flavors: exact-match and semantic-match (the latter has a 90% pass target).

I can update the MAP spreadsheet with these variants. Ben — any items you want to add for operational acceptance?

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>

Subject: Re: Success criteria & acceptance tests — Redwood pilot (AcmeHealth)

Quick add from ops: please include an acceptance test for prefix/KV cache correctness and a regression check for hallucination rate on edge-case prompts. Proposal details:
- KV cache test: run a sequence of 500 stateful multi-turn dialogs and verify token-level continuity (no dropped context) — pass if continuity errors < 1%
- Hallucination regression: run 200 negative-control prompts (where correct answer is empty or 'no-match') and flag > 5% non-empty outputs as a regression.

I'll attach our sample test pack as acceptance-test-cases.pdf (controls + script examples). We should add a short checklist for cutover: feature flags, fallback model, and escalation contact list.

Ben

--
Ben Carter
Sr. Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

Mike / team — thanks, all, for the rapid review. This thread captures the agreed artifacts and owners; please reply with a single-line sign-off if we can lock the MAP and schedule the runs.

Agreed (finalized):
- Latency: warmed 95th < 350ms, cold 95th < 700ms
- Cost: target band $0.45–0.75 per 1k tokens depending on quant profile (Redwood to document exact profile)
- Accuracy: report exact-match and semantic-match; semantic-match target = 90%, exact-match target = 88%
- UAT: 20 reviewers, >= 90% positive responses
- KV/continuity: continuity errors < 1% on 500 multi-turn dialogs
- Hallucination regression: negative-control non-empty outputs <= 5%
- Availability: >= 99.5% during pilot window

Timeline (final):
- 03/03: Redwood delivers MAP and test harness (done)
- 03/05 EOD: Acme delivers 250 annotated examples and access credentials (Mike)
- Week of 03/08: Joint acceptance runs (48–72h)
- 03/11: Steering review, decision & sign-off

Artifacts: MAP-draft-v1.xlsx, acceptance-test-cases.pdf, drive folder (link in spreadsheet). We'll also circulate a short DocuSign for a one-time evaluation addendum (link provided below).

If you confirm delivery of the annotated set by 03/05 EOD, Jordan and I will kick off the runs on 03/08 morning.

One-line sign-off (example): "Acme confirms delivery and we approve MAP as-is"

Thanks,
Hannah
